# Code Style for This Book {#sec-style .unnumbered}

Consistency in the listings is part of the teaching. These are the rules the scripts follow.

## Structure

Every script opens with a block comment stating its chapter, its goal, and any assets it expects to exist. Sections are separated by a ruled comment line so a reader can navigate by scrolling.

```javascript
/**
 * CHAPTER N | Short title
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Goal
 *   One or two sentences on what this produces.
 *
 * Asset dependencies
 *   Anything the reader must import before running.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// STEP 1. What this block does
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

## Comments carry decisions, not translations

A comment that restates the code is noise. A comment that records why one option was chosen over another is the reason the book exists.

```javascript
// Poor: selects band 8
var nir = image.select('B8');

// Better: B8 is the wide near infrared band at 10 m. B8A is narrower and
// better calibrated but only 20 m, so B8 wins wherever spatial detail
// matters more than radiometric precision.
var nir = image.select('B8');
```

## Naming

`camelCase` for variables and functions. `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for values a reader is expected to change at the top of a script, such as `START_YEAR` and `CLOUD_THRESHOLD`. Descriptive over short: `cloudFreeComposite` beats `img2`.

## Chaining

Break long chains across lines with the dot leading each continuation, indented two spaces. Automatic semicolon insertion makes the alternative fragile.

```javascript
var filtered = collection
  .filterDate(START, END)
  .filterBounds(aoi)
  .filter(ee.Filter.lt('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', CLOUD_THRESHOLD));
```

## Parameters

Use named arguments wherever a function accepts them. Positional arguments are compact and unreadable six months later.

```javascript
// Prefer this
var samples = image.sampleRegions({
  collection: points,
  properties: ['landcover'],
  scale: 10
});
```

## Annotations in the printed listings

Where a listing needs numbered commentary, the code block in the chapter carries `// <1>` markers followed by a numbered list. Those markers stay out of the runnable `.js` files, which keep their prose comments instead.
